quarterly_data.signal: Interim CFO Cecile Guegan: Q2 2026 revenue was $15 billion, a year-over-year operational increase of 1%; excluding COVID products the underlying business grew 5% operationally; adjusted diluted EPS $0.77 and reported loss per share of $0.04.

Interim CFO: launched and acquired products delivered $3.2 billion in revenue, up 18% operationally (27% excluding one-time items in Q2 2025); CEO Albert Bourla: acquired-product revenue grew 25% operationally excluding one-time items, and the legacy Seagen portfolio grew 21% in the U.S. excluding the prior-year stocking benefit.
quarterly_data.figure: launched and acquired products $3.2 billion, +18% operationally

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CFO: Q2 adjusted gross margin 76%; adjusted operating expenses $6.1 billion (+4% operationally), with adjusted SI&A down 3% and adjusted R&D up 12% (oncology and obesity candidates); adjusted operating margin 35%; Q2 operating cash flow $3.45 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted gross margin 76%; adjusted operating margin 35%

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CFO: Q2 GAAP results include $4.3 billion of non-cash intangible asset impairments, reflecting the Phase III readout for SV in second-line-plus non-small cell lung cancer and, to a lesser extent, the removal of the revenue projection for Vabryda after a recent discussion with the FDA.

Interim CFO: full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised by $500 million at the midpoint to $60.5 billion-$62.5 billion (from $59.5 billion-$60.5 billion), with COVID-19 revenue now expected at approximately $4 billion, down from $5 billion; adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $2.80-$3 reaffirmed, absorbing an approximately $0.10 impact from the Innovent Biologics transaction; adjusted gross margin expected in the mid-70s range.

Interim CFO: non-COVID performance led to an incremental $1.5 billion above the original guidance, from key products including ELIQUIS and from launched and acquired products, with very strong performance on NURTEC and PADCEV; international COMIRNATY business is mostly secured through government contracts, including the EC.
quarterly_data.figure: incremental $1.5 billion above the original guidance

quarterly_data.signal: Cost programs (Interim CFO / CEO): on track to deliver most of $7.2 billion of net cost savings by end-2026; expanded programs add approximately $2.5 billion of net savings from 2027 through 2029 ($1 billion from technology and simplification in SI&A, approximately $1.5 billion from the next phase of manufacturing optimization); total net savings approximately $9.7 billion through 2029; $700 million of Phase I manufacturing savings expected this year, $175 million realized in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $9.7 billion total net savings through 2029

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Albert Bourla: clear line of sight to a risk-adjusted, high single-digit revenue CAGR from year-end 2028 through year-end 2033, based on in-line products and 20 key potential new medicines and vaccines; Interim CFO: she believes Pfizer is well positioned to return to growth from 2029 onwards.
quarterly_data.figure: high single-digit revenue CAGR from year-end 2028 through year-end 2033

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CFO: the Innovent Biologics deal closed in July, with an acquired in-process R&D charge to be recorded in Q3. CEO: most of Pfizer's business development investment since 2022 has been placed in three transactions, all three performing very well; further deals expected to be bolt-ons, in areas including oncology, immunoinflammation, primary care with obesity and vaccines.

Berobenatide (Metsera; CEO and CSO Chris Boshoff): Pfizer targets a first approval in 2028 and plans 10 Phase III studies in 2026, including a switch study from weekly therapies to monthly dosing; three Phase III trials are ongoing (VESPER-4 and VESPER-5 of weekly dosing now fully enrolled, VESPER-6 monthly); Phase IIb VESPER-3 at the 4.8 mg monthly dose achieved placebo-corrected weight loss of up to 12.3%, and VESPER-1 extension participants at 2.4 mg weekly achieved approximately 16% mean weight loss over 32 weeks. CEO: the obesity market is expected to reach $150 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: placebo-corrected weight loss up to 12.3%; approximately 16% over 32 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Amylin program (CSO Chris Boshoff): Phase I/IIa data for PF-08653945 monotherapy and the nirubenatide combination expected this year; Phase IIb Solace 1 has enrolled more than half of approximately 900 planned participants, with data expected in 2027.

NURTEC (CEO Albert Bourla): strong year-over-year growth and continued leadership of the oral CGRP class in total prescriptions; a Phase III trial in menstrual migraine and a redosing trial are underway, and a pivotal trial start in chronic migraine is expected this year.

R&D output (CEO / CSO): so far in 2026 three regulatory approvals, six key data readouts and eight pivotal study starts; in oncology over the past two years a dozen late-stage study starts, 21 late-stage readouts and six approvals; over the next 12 months Pfizer expects five regulatory decisions, eight key readouts and 19 pivotal study starts.
quarterly_data.figure: next 12 months: five regulatory decisions, eight key readouts, 19 pivotal study starts

quarterly_data.signal: LITFULO (CSO Chris Boshoff): in the Phase III TRANQUILLO program in non-segmental vitiligo both the 50 mg and 100 mg doses delivered significant improvements over placebo on the co-primary endpoints; at 100 mg the placebo-adjusted facial VASI 75 response rate was 19.5% at week 52; full data to be presented at a conference later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: placebo-adjusted facial VASI 75 of 19.5% at week 52

quarterly_data.signal: PADCEV (CSO Chris Boshoff): last month the FDA expanded the approved indication of PADCEV plus pembrolizumab to muscle-invasive bladder cancer regardless of cisplatin eligibility, based on a 35% reduction in the risk of death; a Phase III trial in bladder-sparing muscle-invasive bladder cancer was initiated. Aamir Malik: PADCEV grew over 20% in Q2 and la/mUC new patient share is now above 60%; growth will moderate in la/mUC, with upside from MIBC.
quarterly_data.figure: 35% reduction in the risk of death; new patient share above 60%

quarterly_data.signal: SV (CSO Chris Boshoff): the Phase III primary overall survival endpoint was not met in the intention-to-treat non-squamous NSCLC population; patients with one prior line showed median survival of 13.6 months with SV versus 11.1 months with docetaxel; updated Phase I data of SV plus pembrolizumab in first-line high PD-L1 NSCLC show an unconfirmed objective response rate of about 82%.

4404 PD-1 x VEGF bispecific (CSO Chris Boshoff): since in-licensing from 3SBio about a year ago, Pfizer started nine trials including two Phase III studies, with approximately 230 patients dosed outside China; at the selected pivotal dose in first-line PD-L1 positive NSCLC, 4404 monotherapy generated a confirmed response rate of about 68% and median progression-free survival of about 12.4 months.
quarterly_data.figure: confirmed response rate about 68%; median PFS about 12.4 months

quarterly_data.signal: Mevrometostat (EZH2 inhibitor; CSO Chris Boshoff): three pivotal studies underway; the first readout, MEV-Pro1 (plus XTANDI in post-abiraterone metastatic hormone-resistant prostate cancer), is expected in the fourth quarter based on the current event rate; the trial is fully enrolled and has not reached its events; the statistical plan is based on a clinically meaningful benefit of approximately 30% over standard of care; Phase I showed a 49% reduction in risk of progression or death. Aamir Malik: it would be a 100% global opportunity for Pfizer.
quarterly_data.figure: MEV-Pro1 readout expected in the fourth quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Atirmociclib (CSO Chris Boshoff): randomized Phase II hazard ratio of 0.6, a 40% reduction in risk of progression or death; focus on first-line ER-positive breast cancer and the adjuvant setting, with the adjuvant study expected to start by the end of 2026.

Tilrekimig (IL-4/IL-13/TSLP tri-specific; CSO Chris Boshoff): prior atopic dermatitis data showed 52% and 50% placebo-adjusted EASI-75; Pfizer hopes to start four Phase III studies, including one against placebo and one head-to-head against DUPIXENT powered for superiority, plus asthma and COPD programs.
ADC pipeline (CSO Chris Boshoff): next-wave ADCs in the clinic include GPS, with an Auristatin S payload designed for improved tolerability, and 3028 from Innovent, a bispecific dual payload ADC.

CEO Albert Bourla on AI: Pfizer is already seeing benefits from AI in reducing cost and expanding yields in manufacturing and in commercial effectiveness; the ambition is an AI-native R&D organization.

CEO Albert Bourla: Pfizer's voluntary agreement with the U.S. government to lower drug costs is the continuation of the memorandum of understanding signed at the White House that resolved the MFN and tariffs issue; the agreements are consistent with those of other companies.

CEO Albert Bourla on COVID: vaccine sales are relatively independent of infection rates, while PAXLOVID is now completely correlated with infection rates; this year's very low COVID season was offset by the rest of the business. Interim CFO: low COVID-19 incidence could continue to limit PAXLOVID utilization.
